method: First reasoned review from the provided bytes: atomscan, cleave facts including decoded text, and rizin x86 control-flow disassembly. Static analysis only; samples were never executed. Scanner scores, prior review records and filenames do not prove behavior.
judgment: MALICIOUS for all three: preserved unsolicited persistence, service-DLL replacement and remote injection code. Resource damage limits deployability, but the live mode-3 branch still contains Active Setup registration, self-copy/relaunch and shell cleanup. No ordinary installer or application purpose accounts for this combination.
shared_execution_paths: All outer code bytes at file 0x1000..0x289a have SHA256 98f975dd8b8d9f2e6da736754ef8f87a112e7f7e5f4d104b3f5e385e525c70c4. Entry VA 0x402674 calls dispatcher 0x401cb0. Mode DWORD at file 0x4120 is 3 in all three; dispatcher 0x401f75..0x401f8f selects 0x401900 then 0x401390.

0x401900 constructs a GUID-named HKLM Active Setup Installed Components entry. It writes an expandable StubPath pointing to an EXE path at 0x401a4b, reads its own module through fopen/fseek/ftell/fread, patches the copied bytes, writes them through fwrite at 0x401b26 and launches the new path through CreateProcessA at 0x401b7e.

Cleanup 0x401390 obtains its own module path at 0x4013a7, converts it to an 8.3 path at 0x4013c4, reads COMSPEC, appends /c del and its own path plus > nul, then calls CreateProcessA at 0x4014b8 and ResumeThread at 0x4014d9.

Alternative mode 1 extracts resource type DLL, ID 101 through 0x402460. That helper finds, sizes, loads and locks the resource, copies those bytes into an allocation and calls writer 0x4023c0. The writer passes the bytes to CreateFileA/WriteFile at 0x402409. This is a local resource chain, not a network download.

0x401260 constructs %SystemRoot%/System32/StormServer.dll, opens HKLM/SYSTEM/CurrentControlSet/Services/LanmanServer/Parameters at 0x401310, deletes ServiceDLL at 0x401320 and sets its replacement value at 0x40133e. Mode 1 calls it at 0x401e6a; mode 3 does not select it on the initial dispatch.

0x401150 selects a calc/notepad/Internet Explorer child, calls CreateProcessA, obtains remote memory through VirtualAllocEx, writes the DLL pathname through WriteProcessMemory, resolves Kernel32!LoadLibraryA through GetModuleHandleA/GetProcAddress, then supplies the returned export and remote path buffer to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.

Alternative mode 2 has self-copy, automatic-start service creation and a service dispatcher that extracts and injects the DLL. These alternate capabilities establish retained code, not observed successful execution of those branches.
damage_and_encoding: 824fe666b3d9 and 42ea7ae99977 have entirely zero-filled 40032-byte resource contents at 0x5000..0xec60, including the resource directory. FindResource cannot recover an embedded DLL from those bytes.

f018cda73809 retains a DLL at file 0x5060 of size 39936 bytes; only 2200 of its bytes are nonzero. Its import table and nearly all code are erased, and VA 0x1000741a entry disassembles as zero-byte add instructions. It retains Storm DNS/command and HTTP/API strings, which establish identity/references, not working C2, DDoS, downloading or privilege adjustment.

42ea7ae99977 has a 256-byte .hf W+X section at RVA 0xf000 with entropy about 7.20. Entry remains 0x2674; no direct branch from the preserved loader code targets it, and raw disassembly does not reveal a coherent routine. No unpacker or additional payload behavior is inferred.

All three retain legacy bound/resolved IAT values; GUID text overwrites portions of FirstThunk. Self-copy patch offsets 0x6a0 and 0x3058 reflect a different disk layout. Successful loading, persistence or cleanup on a particular Windows environment was not demonstrated.

The only decoded-string fact is UrlDecode applied to the printf GUID template {%08X-%04X-%04x-...}. It is an engine-generated mechanical decoding observation, not an encoded endpoint or evidence of network contact. No YAML shadow or exception was added.
No cryptographic file encryption, ransom demand, credential theft, Remcos or WannaCry behavior was found. These collector filenames are not reliable program identification.

external_corroboration.scope: Microsoft describes the same StormServer.dll/LanmanServer ServiceDLL replacement and Internet Explorer injection. This corroborates a Shtormec-like lineage; behavior and verdict here are independently derived from the bytes. Its driver overwrite and anti-AV claims were not transferred to these damaged samples.
external_corroboration.triage: All three user-provided tria.ge pages were inaccessible through the web tool; their scores were not used as proof.

yaml_changes: Move servicedll-registry-write-api-cluster from os/service/create to os/registry/write with matcher, defaults and downgrade scope unchanged. Start/dispatch APIs can satisfy the rule without CreateService, so its required result is registry writing. No exact-ID consumers existed.

Ancestor-selector audit found no service/create-only or service/host directory consumers. The broad registry/write consumer is SilentCleanup UAC logic, which separately requires task-path, HKCU Environment and windir property evidence with proximity. All provided samples and mutation controls remain free of that unrelated finding. The new ancestor membership describes a registry-write observation; no package exemption was introduced.

Remove unsupported T1027.009 from generic PE resource access; T1574.002 from an unimported LoadLibraryA string; inherited T1071.001 from generic URLMon references; and T1134.001 from the SeShutdownPrivilege name. Ordinary APIs and references alone do not establish these attack mechanisms.

Make the complete System32 image-path observation notable, describe DLL/EXE/SYS coverage, and constrain its path syntax so doubled source escapes are not read as unescaped paths. Retain the existing escaped-path trait separately.
Require a directory boundary after C:/Windows/System so that it no longer matches the System prefix of System32. This is a matcher correction, not a severity-based suppression.
controls: check.py produces nine byte-mutation and path-boundary cases. Removing CreateService preserves the registry-write observation while removing the create-service import; removing ServiceDLL or RegSetValueExA removes the moved profile. DLL/EXE/nested SYS paths remain notable, escaped paths and TXT files do not match the unescaped image rule, and System32 does not match System. Full reports stay in scratch.
